userStories.title: P1.6c remainder — distinct no-apps / network / permission error surfaces for the unified setup operation
userStories.description: As a user setting up or re-templating a workspace, I want no-apps-available, network-error and permission-denial failures to be visibly distinct when I preview or apply a template, so that I never lose my template choice and always know what actually failed.
acceptanceCriteria: C2 contract (PLAN.md, verbatim): "No apps available, network error and permission denial must have distinct UI, without losing template choice."

`ApplyTemplateErrorCode` gains the missing codes additively (permission / no-apps-available discriminator) so preview and apply results can tell the three failure kinds apart — the server contract addition US-027 recorded as a separate slice ("the preview query exposes no error discriminator (`useWorkspaceTemplatePreview` returns `error` but the component renders the same 'Preview unavailable' panel), and `ApplyTemplateErrorCode` has no permission code")

The preview/apply front components render a distinct panel per failure kind (no apps available vs network error vs permission denial) instead of the single "Preview unavailable" panel, and the template choice is preserved in all three
Empty-catalogue protection stays intact (US-027): `shouldAutoSkipInstallAppsStep` cannot auto-skip on an errored catalogue — template choice cannot be discarded

P1.6c bullet (PLAN.md, verbatim) remains satisfied by the existing US-026/US-027 work — reuse it, do not rebuild: "preview apps, prerequisites, samples and customization; allow blank/CRM, optional app exclusion, continue with successful steps and retry later. Empty catalogue cannot discard template choice. Both entrypoints use the same operation."
Additive only: no rename/removal of existing error codes, DTO fields or GraphQL surface; hand-written preview/operation documents stay in place (the `graphql:generate` switch is orchestrator Tier 2)

Starting state: partial — US-026 (preview resolved states) and US-027 (partial-failure truth + retry + empty-catalogue) are done-for-review in docs/plan/phases/phase-01-report.md; this story is that report's explicitly named next executor slice

userStories.title: P9.2b saved runs — authorized persisted results with zero-provider-call re-open, scoped by the twenty-shared cache contract
userStories.description: As a user re-opening a saved AI run, I want the authorized result to come back with zero provider calls, so that re-reading my work never costs money or leaks scope.
acceptanceCriteria: "Saved runs persist authorized results; reopening them makes zero provider calls." (PLAN.md P9.2b verbatim)

"Test workspace switching, changed permissions and expired results" (PLAN.md verbatim) — a saved run from another workspace, after a role/permission change (ACCESS_CHANGED/KEY_MISMATCH), or past expiry (EXPIRED) never resolves, per the `twenty-shared/src/ai` contract (`evaluateAiResultReuse` reasons FRESH/KEY_MISMATCH/NOT_REVIEWED/EXPIRED/VERSION_MISMATCH/ACCESS_CHANGED)
"an explicit rerun is a separate user action with a visible cost estimate" (PLAN.md verbatim) — rerun is never implicit and always surfaces the estimate before executing

Implementation sits against the stable `twenty-shared/src/ai` contract location (orchestrator re-queue note, verbatim: "Re-queue against the stable `twenty-shared/src/ai` contract location") — pure domain + types + tests there, mirroring the US-043 barrel/type/utils structure

The P7-gated `a2e-accounting` `aiCacheEntry` object and `score-subventions` are NOT touched (US-043 learning: app-side wiring is P7-gated; app logic functions cannot import twenty-shared) — no workspace-object migration

"Private results can only resolve to scoped keys" (US-043 contract); only reviewed public-catalogue results may resolve globally (C6, verbatim: "only public-only catalogue results may be shared globally after review")
Saved-run re-open makes no new provider call and no new quota consumption is billed for the cached read (C6 verbatim: "Saved-run re-open must incur no new provider call")
